checks.finding: With U=G12[S], a=Hi, b=pJ and ba=1, q=1-ab is idempotent, qa=bq=0. A(x,y)=(ax+qy,by) has inverse (w,z)->(bw,az+qw); both composites are identity. This calculation is valid for arbitrary unital R with central Laurent variable.

Sufficient exact conditions are (e²-e)i12=0, p2(e²-e)=0, p0 e i2=0 and p2 e i0=0. Since HJ=JH=1+(2-t-t^-1)(e²-e), these imply ba=1, p2q=0, q i2=0 and J i2 has image in U. These are the actual equations needed from propagation margins, not a consequence of width alone without specifying where idempotence fails.

A and its inverse have finite exponent ranges. On G2 the inverse is J with no q component, giving the exact positive cutoff 1 and negative cutoff -1. On B sufficiently remote tails follow from finite exponent bounds. The two Laurent half-images are complementary. The given intersection argument proves their quotient images are complementary after removing the corresponding tails; no basis of either summand is assumed.

The actual finite matrix can be written P=pi A pr_nonnegative A^-1 j_C. Every basis input of finite C involves finitely many Laurent coefficients. Its two image/kernel summands are the quotient half-images, so P²=P. The outer half-degree decomposition using ex and t^-1(1-e)x gives P(x)=ex when the stated buffer equations hold.
Multiplication gives E12(-e)E21(e)E12(-e)=[[1-e,-e],[e,1-e]]. Its displayed inverse is correct, and conjugating diag(e,1-e) gives diag(0,1). No projective summand is presumed free.

With coincident basis locations for the two copies, each shear has propagation at most eta; successive partial products have bounds at most 3eta, and the concatenated forward/inverse path at most 6eta. Entrywise cutoff preserves propagation and shear invertibility without preserving idempotence. A core enlarged by the complete intermediate propagation budget gives the original exact identity there.

After retaining e, complementary h+(1-e) equals h+(1-h)+(1-hprime) in the buffered inner identification. The cutoff three-shear conjugation makes that complement geometric in a neighborhood of the 1/3 core. Buffering and finite propagation eliminate all cross entries from core generators, so those generators split off. Together with retained e they are supported within the 2/3 region; the rest has no generators in the 1/3 core.
